finding.claim: The DELETE /projects/:id handler calls authorized(), which returns a boolean, and ignores the result. Any authenticated user can delete any project. Unlike authorize(), authorized() does not throw.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (req.user) sending DELETE /projects/<id> for a project they do not own, with the id in req.params.id.
finding.sink: req.store.projects.delete(project.id) at api.js:19, a destructive operation on another user's project.

trace.note: Project is loaded by id with no ownership filter
authorized(req.user, project) returns false for non-owners, but the return value is discarded and nothing throws

finding.guards_checked: authorized() at api.js:12-14 only returns a boolean. The throwing authorize() at api.js:4-10 is not used on this route. I saw no other middleware in this file, and authentication (req.user) is assumed to be set elsewhere. There is also no check that the project exists: a missing id makes project undefined and the handler throws a TypeError, which is a minor robustness issue and not an authorization bypass.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean only and its result is discarded at api.js:18. The throwing authorize() at api.js:4-10 is used only on the PUT route (api.js:25). No other middleware exists in this file.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls authorized(req.user, project) as a bare statement, so its boolean is ignored, and api.js:19 deletes the project regardless of ownership. Any authenticated non-owner can delete it, and the sibling PUT route correctly uses the throwing authorize() at api.js:25.
